name: NASA Task Load Index – Raw TLX
citation: Hart, S. G., & Staveland, L. E. (1988). Development of NASA-TLX (Task Load Index): Results of empirical and theoretical research. In P. A. Hancock & N. Meshkati (Eds.), Human Mental Workload (pp. 139–183). North-Holland. Raw (unweighted) scoring: Hart, S. G. (2006). NASA-Task Load Index (NASA-TLX); 20 years later. Proc. HFES Annual Meeting, 50(9), 904–908.
license: NASA states that the TLX is 'open source' and may be used and modified without permission. No NASA endorsement is implied.

items.text: Mental Demand — How mentally demanding was the task?
Physical Demand — How physically demanding was the task?
Temporal Demand — How hurried or rushed was the pace of the task?
Performance — How successful were you in accomplishing what you were asked to do?
Effort — How hard did you have to work to accomplish your level of performance?
Frustration — How insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, and annoyed were you?

notes: Raw TLX = unweighted mean of the six subscales (0–100). Verify wording against the official NASA form before a study. The frustration subscale is a partial proxy for interruption annoyance.
